name: Lightsource bp
headquarters: London, United Kingdom (US arm: Denver, CO — Lightsource bp USA)
ownership: wholly owned by bp since Oct 24, 2024 (£400M for the remaining 50.03% + £2.1bn net debt consolidated) — and in play: after the 'Project Scala' 50%-stake process (2025), the FT reported Jul 24, 2026 that bp is in advanced talks to sell the ENTIRE Lightsource business to a Kuwait-backed consortium of Wren House (KIA) + Qualitas Energy; no signing confirmed as of Aug 2026
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Lightsource bp is the second verified Hithium customer in the field — and the cleaner illustration that the relationship lives only where FEOC doesn't reach. The deal: Woolooga BESS Stage 1 in Queensland, Australia — 128 × 5 MWh containers (640 MWh, 314 Ah LFP, 25-year warranties, INTEC partnering on O&M), announced Dec 2024 as Hithium's Australian market entry, with Lightsource BP then named among Hithium's flagship customers in HKEX prospectus coverage (ess-news, Mar 2025). But there is no incumbency lock — the next, larger Queensland battery (Lower Wonga, 281 MW/843 MWh) went to rival Gotion via an INTEC JV — and the US business runs the opposite playbook: ~8.3 GW of FEOC-clean First Solar modules committed through 2028, all-domestic marketing, no US BESS in the public record. The dominant fact about the account is ownership volatility: bp's renewables retreat turned its 2024 acquisition into a 2026 disposal process, the Woolooga asset itself may have moved to Aula Energy (Macquarie) in the Feb 2026 1 GW portfolio sale, and a Kuwaiti-consortium acquisition would reset procurement strategy entirely.
ecosystemRole: We assess Lightsource bp as three different counterparties wearing one brand: (1) in Australia/APAC, a proven Chinese-BESS buyer (Hithium at Woolooga, Gotion at Lower Wonga, CHINT at Goulburn River) pivoting explicitly to hybrids for 'data centre and AI-driven demand'; (2) in the US, a top-tier solar developer (#1 US solar developer, Solar Power World 2025) with hyperscaler PPAs (two with Meta — including Mowata, framed against Meta's Hyperion AI campus in Louisiana; Google's Fort Wayne data-center campus via Honeysuckle; Amazon Ohio; Microsoft) whose supply chain is deliberately FEOC-proof and whose storage business barely exists yet — three development-stage solar+storage projects with no disclosed MWh; (3) at the corporate level, a distressed-strategy asset mid-sale whose signing entity may not own its projects at COD (the sell-down model plus the Aula transfer make warranty/O&M counterparty identity a live diligence question on every deal).

productsAndServices.name: US solar development platform (the hyperscaler franchise)
productsAndServices.description: ~2,730 MW operating across 18 US projects, ~856 MW in construction (led by the 700 MW Jones City Energy Center, TX — Toyota 15-yr VPPA on Jones City 2), ~1,785 MW advanced development. Named offtakers include Google (Honeysuckle 188 MW IN — 'supporting Google's Fort Wayne data center campus'), Meta (Arche 133 MW OH; Mowata 172 MWdc LA, PPA Jul 2026, $237M, framed by trade press against Meta's Hyperion campus in Richland Parish), Amazon (375 MWdc Ohio PPA), Microsoft, Toyota, McDonald's, Verizon, L3Harris, H&M, Allianz, Constellation.
productsAndServices.positioning: #1 US solar developer (Solar Power World 2025); the Gulf-South/Louisiana position adjacent to Meta's AI buildout is the sharpest AIDC asset. US supply chain marketed as American-made: First Solar modules (~8.3 GW committed through 2028), Array Technologies trackers, Nucor steel.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: PPA-first develop-finance-build with sell-downs (JERA Nex bought 395 MW in 2024 with Lightsource retaining asset management; HASI structured equity; Pinnacle tax equity); $5B+ third-party US capital raised since 2019.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers/corporates (a dedicated 'Data Center Solutions' page offers PPAs, JVs, directly connected arrangements, co-location), utilities, C&I.
productsAndServices.roadmap: US storage is the undeveloped leg: Big Bronco (300 MW solar + 300 MW storage, CO), Zion Valley (342 MW, KS) and Golden Plains (150 MW, NE) carry storage components with no disclosed MWh or suppliers — an open procurement whitespace.

productsAndServices.name: APAC hybrid & storage platform (where the Hithium relationship lives)
productsAndServices.description: Australia is the storage proving ground: Woolooga BESS Stage 1 (222 MW/640 MWh, QLD — 128 Hithium 5 MWh containers, construction from Dec 2024, expected operational mid-2026); Goulburn River (585 MWdc solar + 49 MW/562 MWh DC-coupled 8-hr hybrid + a separately announced 450 MW/1,370 MWh standalone battery, NSW — CHINT battery technology and O&M, DT Infrastructure EPC, energization late 2026); Lower Wonga (380 MWdc + 281 MW/843 MWh, QLD — INTEC + Gotion Hi-Tech Australia EPC JV, Rio Tinto hybrid offtake for the Boyne Island smelter, COD late 2028). Feb 2026: five operating solar assets (1,037 MWdc incl. Woolooga solar) plus options over ~800 MW/800 MWh of co-located BESS sold to Aula Energy (Macquarie); retained APAC pipeline 9.5 GW+.
productsAndServices.positioning: The APAC strategy is explicitly 'hybrid renewable projects... for emerging data centre and AI-driven demand' (COO Adam Pegg). Chinese BESS suppliers compete freely here — no FEOC regime — and Lightsource multi-sources them (Hithium, Gotion, CHINT), with INTEC the recurring integration/O&M constant.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: CIS/LTESA revenue support (Australia), corporate hybrid PPAs (Rio Tinto), asset sell-downs (Aula).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Post-sale ownership of the under-construction Woolooga BESS (Lightsource vs Aula) is unresolved in the public record — it determines who Hithium's warranty/O&M counterparty actually is.

productsAndServices.name: UK/Europe development & services
productsAndServices.description: UK heritage business (~2.4 GW developed): Tiln Farm — the company's first co-located BESS globally (25 MW/50 MWh, energized Feb 2024, supplier undisclosed, sold to Schroders Greencoat); Pentir — first UK standalone BESS (57 MW/228 MWh, Wales, consented Oct 2024); Plas Power (57 MWac solar + storage, approved May 2026); Hett Moor (AR7 CfD, Feb 2026). UK O&M/services platform (1.3 GW managed; #3 in UK solar O&M per Wood Mackenzie) put up for separate sale Aug 2025. Iberia: 500 MW solar+storage portfolio marketed.
productsAndServices.positioning: Storage described as 'first of a multi-gigawatt global pipeline' — no GW figure ever disclosed.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Pentir construction timing and supplier selection are open; the O&M platform sale removes a retention argument.

productsAndServices.name: bp integration & the sale process (the meta-story)
productsAndServices.description: bp took 43% in 2017, 50% in 2019, and completed 100% on Oct 24, 2024 (£400M + £2.1bn net debt) — then reset strategy within months: renewables capex cut ~$5B/yr, a $20B divestment program, Elliott Management pressure, and 'Project Scala' (sell 50% of Lightsource; bids due Jun 2025) escalating to reported advanced talks to sell the whole business to Wren House (KIA) + Qualitas Energy (FT via Reuters, Jul 24, 2026). bp CEO churn compounds it: Auchincloss out Dec 2025; Meg O'Neill (ex-Woodside) CEO from Apr 2026. bp flagged $4-5B of Q4 2025 impairments primarily in gas & low-carbon, with press attributing >$4B cumulative to Lightsource + Archaea (split undisclosed).
productsAndServices.positioning: From bp growth engine (Nov 2023 rationale) to divestment asset in ~9 months — the fastest strategy reversal among the Batch B accounts.
productsAndServices.roadmap: A Kuwait-consortium close would re-underwrite every procurement framework; interim decision paralysis is the realistic near-term state.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the Hithium-Lightsource relationship as real, single-deal, and geographically fenced: one 640 MWh Australian contract plus a prospectus naming — with no US or UK extension possible under current rules (the US book is FEOC-clean by design: ~8.3 GW of First Solar modules, all-domestic marketing, ITC-dependent financing) and no Australian incumbency lock (Lower Wonga went to Gotion).

(High confidence) We assess ownership volatility as the dominant account risk: bp is mid-process on selling the entire platform (Wren House/Qualitas reported), the UK O&M arm is separately for sale, and the Woolooga asset itself may now belong to Aula Energy — meaning the counterparty that signed Hithium's contract, the entity that owns the asset at COD, and the owner who decides future procurement may be three different organizations within a year.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the practical Hithium plays as: (1) deliver Woolooga to energization flawlessly — it is the Australian reference asset and the prospectus proof point; (2) chase the retained 9.5 GW+ APAC hybrid pipeline (explicitly aimed at data-center/AI demand) where Chinese supply competes freely and INTEC relationships carry over; (3) track the Aula BESS options (~800 MWh) — the buyer of those options inherits the procurement decision; (4) treat the US storage whitespace (Big Bronco/Zion Valley/Golden Plains, suppliers unnamed) as unwinnable for ITC-claiming vintages absent a FEOC-compliant structure.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AIDC angle as PPA-mediated rather than storage-led today: Google Fort Wayne, two Meta deals against the Hyperion buildout, Amazon Ohio, Microsoft — a first-class hyperscaler rolodex attached to solar, with the storage attach (and its supplier choices) still ahead of it, mostly in APAC first.

(High confidence) For the Hithium lens: Lightsource proves the export-market playbook works — win where FEOC doesn't reach, on price-competitive 5 MWh hardware with long warranties and a local O&M partner — and simultaneously proves its ceiling: no co-marketing gravity, no framework, contestable follow-ons, and a customer whose US half is structurally closed. Weight the account by its APAC pipeline, not its global GW.

relationships.note: Woolooga BESS Stage 1: 128 × 5 MWh containers (640 MWh) — Hithium's Australian market entry, geographically fenced from the FEOC-clean US book.
relationships.context:
The December 2024 deal — 640 MWh of 314 Ah LFP containers with 25-year warranties and INTEC partnering on O&M, expected operational mid-2026 — made Lightsource bp the second verified Hithium field customer, later named among Hithium's flagship customers in HKEX prospectus coverage.

The relationship lives only where FEOC doesn't reach: the US book is FEOC-clean by design (~8.3 GW of First Solar modules), the larger follow-on Queensland battery (Lower Wonga) went to rival Gotion, and the Woolooga asset itself may now belong to Aula Energy after the February 2026 Australian portfolio sale — so the signing entity, the COD owner, and the future procurement decider may be three different organizations.
